title: Germany's BSI raises threat assessment to between 'tense' and 'critical', CHIP Turkey reports
summary: CHIP Türkiye reports that Germany's BSI raised its threat assessment from 'tense' to between 'tense' and 'critical' in its annual report, citing AI-driven attacks and geopolitics. It says the BSI Cyber Index averages 170 (2024 = 100), up 50% year on year, and that about 160 new vulnerabilities appear per day, 35% more than last year. The article says 90% of reported 2025 ransomware cases hit small and medium businesses.
plain: Germany's BSI says the cyber threat is now between 'tense' and 'critical', according to CHIP Türkiye, citing AI-driven attacks and geopolitics.
exec: Germany's cyber agency rates the threat higher, per CHIP Türkiye, with ransomware mostly hitting small and medium businesses.

sources.name: CHIP Türkiye: Almanya'nın yeni siber güvenlik raporunda çarpıcı rakamlar

date_note: Dated by CHIP's article day; the BSI report itself was not read (BSI blocks automated readers).

validation.note: Only CHIP Türkiye read; BSI original not read.

review.note: Checked against CHIP Turkiye (20 Nov): between tense and critical, index 170 (+50%), 160 vulns/day (+35%), 90% of 2025 reported ransomware cases hit SMEs; BSI original unread, stated as CHIP's report
